memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then Aaron's sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, on the burning wood that is on the altar. You are to wash the internal organs and the legs with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.'" - Lev 1:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even the inner organs and the legs — the parts nobody would see, the parts caked with dirt from the field — had to be washed. God cared about what was hidden inside the offering, not only the presentable outside.

That is a searching thought. It is possible to look impressive on the outside while the interior life is unwashed. Jesus said as much to the Pharisees, calling them whitewashed tombs (Mtt 23:27). God has never been satisfied with surface religion. He looks at the heart (1 Sam 16:7).

Then comes the beautiful phrase: an aroma pleasing to the LORD. This is not saying God enjoys the smell of burning meat. It is a picture of divine acceptance — of God receiving something with genuine delight. The smoke rose and God was pleased.

Here is the wonder of the gospel. Paul takes this exact language and applies it to Christ: he loved us and gave himself up for us as a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God (Eph 5:2). And astonishingly, he then says that believers themselves become the pleasing aroma of Christ (2 Cor 2:15).

In Christ, God is not merely tolerating you. He is pleased with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an inner area of my life I have never brought to God for washing?
2. Can I believe that in Christ, God genuinely delights in me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, wash what is hidden in me, not just what others can see. Thank You that through Christ my life can rise to You as something You receive with joy. Amen.
